lines: On Bethany's 129-card ledger (ledger:30d), the stated confidence spans 0.5-0.68 (p10 0.504, p50 0.526, p90 0.566) and scores AUC 0.568 as a classifier of hit, 95% interval 0.47-0.672, Spearman rho 0.118.

That interval straddles 0.5: on this history the stated figure does not demonstrably separate a card that will work from one that will not. Not demonstrably backwards either - the forward test's reversal is not reproduced, and not refuted, by the ledger.

By stated-confidence quintile the hit rate runs 68% (stated 0.5-0.507), 35% (stated 0.507-0.519), 50% (stated 0.519-0.536), 54% (stated 0.537-0.554), 73% (stated 0.556-0.68) from the least to the most confident fifth.

Fitting on the first half by date (64 rows) and scoring the second (65): the curve has 5 level(s) and returns 5 distinct value(s); ECE moves from 8.6 pts to 31.3 pts, AUC from 0.406 to 0.438 - unchanged up to ties, as a monotone map must be.

The forward test's resolved cards at Bethany (202 cards, hit = met the promised rate): AUC 0.296, interval 0.2-0.398, rho -0.315; by quintile 62%, 18%, 10%, 15%, 20%. The reversal the reviewer saw is real on this window.

Calibration and discrimination are different failures. Isotonic regression can move a stated 0.60 onto the observed rate; it is monotone, so it cannot reorder cards, and the AUC after equals the AUC before. The reviewer's question is discrimination, and no curve fitted to these rows answers it.

No cell clears every bar (a governed fit above the registry floor, ECE under 0.05 out of sample, and an AUC interval above 0.5). Nothing is published; the cards keep the basis they have, the UI keeps the figure hidden, and the admission floor stays off every non-isotonic basis.
